rationale: A 13-year-old girl with solitary cysticercosis of the parotid gland diagnosed by FNAC. There is no central nervous system or intracranial involvement, representing an extracranial soft-tissue non-target condition.

evidence_items.source_quote: A diagnosis of cysticercosis of parotid gland was made.

rationale: An 18-year-old female presenting with diplopia and globe retraction due to isolated medial rectus extraocular muscle cysticercosis. There was no intracranial or central nervous system involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: Ultrasound B-scan [Fig. 2] showed a grossly thickened medial rectus muscle with a cystic lesion and a high reflective spot (scolex) within suggestive of medial rectus muscle cysticercosis.

rationale: A 32-year-old female presenting with a left supraclavicular mass diagnosed as subcutaneous cysticercosis on fine-needle aspiration. There was no neurological symptom or central nervous system involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: A diagnosis of subcutaneous cysticercosis was made, and medication/excision of the swelling was advised.

rationale: An institutional report describing the design and implementation of postgraduate educational health programs at Lurio University in Mozambique. Not a clinical case report of an individual human patient.

rationale: Case 2 in a two-case series: An 18-year-old female presenting with eclamptic seizures and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Neurocysticercosis is not diagnosed or evaluated for this patient.

rationale: A 32-year-old male with isolated ocular subretinal/subchoroidal cysticercosis with scolices confirmed on ultrasound and histology following trans-scleral excision. There was no central nervous system or intracranial involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: The suggested histologic diagnosis was that of ocular cysticercosis.

rationale: A 30-year-old female presenting with a tongue mass diagnosed as lingual cysticercosis on surgical histopathology. Brain CT was explicitly performed and confirmed the absence of neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathological examination revealed cysticercosis cellulosae in tongue musculature [Figure 4].

rationale: A 28-year-old male with skeletal muscle cysticercosis of the calf confirmed on surgical excision and histopathology showing Taenia solium. There was no central nervous system or intracranial involvement.

rationale: A 46-year-old male diagnosed with isolated intramuscular cysticercosis of the left biceps muscle on high-resolution ultrasonography. There was no central nervous system or intracranial involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was diagnosed with isolated intramuscular cysticercosis and subsequently underwent conservative treatment with anthelmintic albendazole for 1 month.

rationale: A 13-year-old boy presenting with diminution of vision and redness in the left eye due to an anterior chamber live worm identified as Taenia solium. Non-contrast CT of the head and orbit was completely normal, confirming isolated ocular cysticercosis without CNS or neurocysticercosis involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was also advised for non-contrast-enhanced computerized tomography (NECT) of the head and orbit which yielded normal reports.

rationale: A 60-year-old woman presenting with a right supraclavicular mass diagnosed as racemose cysticercosis upon excision and histopathology. No central nervous system involvement or neurological symptoms were present, representing isolated extracranial soft tissue cysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the above findings of gross and microscopic examination, a diagnosis of racemose cysticercosis was made.

rationale: A 21-year-old male with an ocular adnexal mass below the inner corner of the left eye. Excisional biopsy confirmed cysticercus cellulosae with scolex. There were no neurological symptoms or central nervous system lesions.

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathological features confirmed the diagnosis of cysticercosis.

rationale: A 27-year-old male presenting with a subcutaneous back swelling. Excisional biopsy confirmed subcutaneous cysticercosis cellulosae. There was no central nervous system or neurological involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: A final diagnosis of subcutaneous cysticercosis was made.

rationale: A 5-year-old boy presenting with a subcutaneous chest wall swelling confirmed as cysticercus cellulosae by excision biopsy. CT scan of the head was unremarkable, confirming absence of neurocysticercosis.
step4_condition_matched: Subcutaneous chest wall cysticercosis without CNS involvement

evidence_items.source_quote: CT scan head and ophthalmic examination were were unremarkable.

rationale: A 12-year-old girl with an abdominal wall subcutaneous cyst confirmed as cysticercosis. Brain imaging did not reveal any foci of neurocysticercosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Further investigations did not reveal any foci of cysticercosis in the brain or eye.

rationale: A 33-year-old female with a lower lip mass diagnosed with labial cysticercosis upon excision. Brain MRI showed no evidence of cysticerci in the brain or eye, confirming isolated oral cysticercosis without central nervous system involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed no evidence of cysticerci in the brain or eye.

rationale: A 57-year-old male presenting with a right parotid mass. FNA biopsy revealed a degenerated cestode structure in the parotid gland confirmed by CDC. No central nervous system involvement or neurological symptoms were present.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, a single degenerated structure suspicious for the neck, scolex, and partial strobila of the cestode was identified (Figure 2).

rationale: A 31-year-old woman presenting with progressive memory loss and frontal lobe mass effect on MRI with elevated choline on MR spectroscopy. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned, evaluated, or diagnosed in this case report.
step4_condition_matched: Non-target condition (frontal lobe lesion / gliomatosis cerebri)

evidence_items.source_quote: Computerised tomography of the brain revealed mild left hemispheric mass effects.

rationale: A 4-year-old male presenting with a superficial abdominal wall mass. FNA cytology demonstrated a solitary detached hooklet of cysticercus confirming subcutaneous cysticercosis, and imaging techniques ruled out lesions at other sites including the CNS.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient also underwent imaging techniques, and lesions at other sites were ruled out.

rationale: A patient presenting with a right neck mass diagnosed as cysticercosis of the sternocleidomastoid muscle based on ultrasound and CT demonstrating a scolex in the muscle. There was no central nervous system involvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the pathognomonic ultrasonographic and supportive CT scan findings, the diagnosis of cysticercosis of the right sternocleidomastoid muscle was made.

rationale: A 15-year-old male presenting with a subcutaneous cyst over the right nasal bridge. Excision confirmed cysticercosis larvae with scolex. No neurological symptoms or central nervous system lesions were present.

rationale: A 19-year-old male with an idiopathic pigmented vitreous cyst in the left eye. Serological testing definitively ruled out cysticercosis, and no central nervous system lesions were present.

evidence_items.source_quote: The ultimate diagnosis indicated a primary (idiopathic) pigmented vitreous cyst.

rationale: This text segment is a partial case presentation describing a 56-year-old male presenting with chronic headaches, pork consumption, and past VP shunt, but ends prior to any neuroimaging, laboratory workup, pathology, or diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.

rationale: A 19-year-old female on anti-tubercular therapy presenting with paradoxical CNS tuberculomas. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned, evaluated, or diagnosed in this case presentation.

evidence_items.source_quote: Final diagnosis: Paradoxical CNS tuberculomas in a patient with PTB on ATT and pre-existing epilepsy.

rationale: A 60-year-old male presenting with headache and confusion found to have CNS tuberculomas mimicking brain metastases, confirmed by choroidal tubercles on fundus examination. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned or evaluated.

evidence_items.source_quote: Final diagnosis: CNS tuberculomas mimicking multiple brain metastases.

rationale: A 28-year-old female presenting with acute left-sided hemiparesis diagnosed with CNS tuberculoma and tuberculous meningitis positive for M. tuberculosis on CBNAAT. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned or evaluated.

evidence_items.source_quote: Final diagnosis: CNS tuberculoma with tuberculous meningitis mimicking acute ischemic stroke.

rationale: A 22-year-old male presenting with subacute memory loss diagnosed with a thalamic tuberculoma responding to anti-tubercular therapy. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned or evaluated in this case.

evidence_items.source_quote: Clinical pearl: In young patients with isolated subacute memory loss, CNS TB should be considered, as thalamic tuberculomas can mimic degenerative or vascular disorders.

rationale: A 26-year-old female with epilepsy presenting with breakthrough seizures and fever diagnosed with multiple ring-enhancing tuberculomas and tuberculous meningitis. Neurocysticercosis is not mentioned or evaluated.

evidence_items.source_quote: Final diagnosis: CNS tuberculomas with tuberculous meningitis presenting as recurrent seizures in a patient with epilepsy.
